fields.title: Use inheritable configuration properties instead of traditional connection strings
fields.decision: Configure connection attributes as discrete properties in the Hereditary Configuration Hierarchy; allow a child to inherit a parent value and override it at a lower level.
fields.context: Applications can need many database and shard connections, with separate read and write endpoints and many repeated values. Repeating complete connection strings makes that fleet difficult to manage.

alternatives.option: Traditional connection strings configured independently for every connection.
alternatives.whyRejected: They repeat common values across a large connection fleet; the document adopts inheritance specifically to reduce that redundancy and make many connections manageable.

fields.consequences: A global, database, shard-set, shard, or endpoint setting can supply a value; read/write-specific values can differ only where necessary. Secrets can remain outside source through the .NET configuration system.
